title: A surface counterexample to Shafarevich holomorphic convexity
main_claim: There is a smooth projective surface X with a connected nodal curve Z_0 of smooth rational curves such that im(pi_1(Z_0) -> pi_1(X)) is infinite. So the universal cover of X is not holomorphically convex, which disproves the Shafarevich conjecture in dimension 2.

issues.description: The tail meridian is identified with 'base circuit followed by one full pair-boundary loop, up to conjugacy and the choice of multiplication convention' without a detailed homotopy. I rebuilt it: the loop (u, cu) with |c|>1 lives in S^1 x annulus with pi_1=Z^2, so it equals the base loop at constant w=R times one pair-boundary loop. The constant-w loop is homotopic to the q(0) section loop, because all marking motions stay inside small pair disks. Both factors are killed, so the argument holds; it is only terse.
issues.evidence: pi_1(neighbourhood of D_* minus the horizontal sections) is free of rank 24 with m_2=m_1^{-1} on each tail. This matches Pi_pair, consistent with the lemma.

coverage:
I read every section in full: weighted GS criterion, family and based monodromy, three double covers, pinching, shift basis, involution presentation, transfer, deep monodromy relators, parameter cover, compactification, distinguished fiber meridians, local detection and descent, rational special fiber, and the retraction argument.

What I re-derived or checked:
- Lemma degree-one: 5 invariant characters, including the chi_j covers being unramified at 0 and the iota lift fixing the sheet.
- The weight-3 estimate on the c_j.
- The cyclic-endpoint argument (T^4 = id, w_3 appears once as the first letter), the T_2 propagation identity, and the sigma propagation identity.
- The Frattini computation of d, and C + dC = R. I brute-forced this over F_2[(Z/4)^2] for all b with b mod 2 != 0 and all choices of v: rank 16 in every case.
- The identity P = (1+t)G.
- The GS numerics at t = 49/200: G > 1.028, total < -1/125, and a finite J (about 579) makes the monodromy cost < 1/100.
- The transfer lemma via the L ⋊ H operator representation.
- The Phi|_K = core-collapse identification, and the orientation in sigma(a_h) = a_{b-h}^{-1}.
- b_j not in 2H.
- K -> Pi surjectivity, and that the pinching square gives theta beta_m = theta.
- E_0 closed, so it contains D_J.
- Invariance under gamma_*^2 via full twists.
- The main-component meridian as a section loop.
- Local detection: N ∩ gA_Vg^{-1} = 1 kills all D_X meridians, including exceptional ones.
- The local models at D_* (the cover is smooth and SNC there, so no resolution happens), main lifts have degree 1, tail lifts are z^d.
- Density in N, the retraction plus properness step, and Lemma rational-hull.

Consistency checks: the necessary Hodge-theoretic constraints (zero image of H_1(Z_0, Q), FAb-type condition on Q) follow automatically and are not violated. Given the size of the claim, expert review of the Section 3 geometry would still be prudent.
sibling_notes: The sibling 'A projective fourfold with large fundamental group and non-Stein universal cover' (rank 88) was also no_gap_found. No shared lemmas were needed: this paper is self-contained apart from standard citations (SGA1, Stacks, Encinas–Hauser, Lojasiewicz). It cites companion OpenAI papers only in the consequences remarks, not in the proof.
